title: Write TLV datasets into a composite field

blocks.text: The acquirer is moving its e-commerce traffic to the network's 2023 link, and the network's certification team sends back its first findings: purchases with a long authentication payload arrive unreadable, and one test message made the gateway throw instead of sending anything. The gateway builds DE 34 and DE 104 itself, because jPOS 2.1.7 carries them as plain bytes.
`CompositeWriter.write` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/CompositeWriter.java` already loops over the datasets. Finish the two methods marked `TODO`:

items: `content`: a TLV dataset's elements, as bytes;
`envelope`: the dataset, as it goes into the field.

blocks.text: Tags are given as numbers, such as `0x9C` or `0xDF8117`, and are written with as many bytes as they need. Refuse with an `IllegalArgumentException`. About twenty-five lines in total.

cases.says: each dataset is written as its identifier, a two-byte length and its BER-TLV elements, in the order given, with one-, two- and three-byte tags
00, FF and bitmap-range identifiers are refused for a TLV dataset
a value of 128 bytes or more gets the 81 or 82 length form, not a single length byte
a dataset over 255 bytes has both bytes of its length written, most significant first
0x70 is still a TLV dataset identifier and 0x71 is not
a dataset longer than the 516 bytes TLVList.pack() can write in jPOS 2.1.7 is still written whole
content of exactly 65535 bytes fits, and one byte more is refused instead of written with a wrong length

origin.section: 17.6. A Writer Encodes Every Length Itself, Because the Packager Sees Only Bytes

concepts: A composite field is a row of datasets, each a one-byte identifier, a two-byte big-endian length counting its content, and the content; the field prefix, dataset lengths and TLV lengths must agree.
The writer encodes every length itself: BER long forms from 128 bytes, a two-byte dataset length up to 65535, and no TLVList.pack() with its 516-byte buffer.
